topic: Intervals of convergence with endpoint checks

problems.desc: Part (c): a correct response states the interval as all real numbers and says why no endpoint test is needed --- an infinite radius leaves no endpoints to check. Full credit connects that to the ratio computation rather than only quoting the answer.

Part (c): a correct response tests both endpoints separately --- at the right endpoint the series becomes the harmonic series and diverges, at the left endpoint it becomes the alternating harmonic series and converges --- and reports the interval as closed on the left and open on the right. Full credit names which series each endpoint produces.

problems.slot: the sum at the right endpoint

problems.desc: Part (c): a correct response finds that BOTH endpoints converge here --- one gives a convergent p-series and the other its alternating version --- so the interval is closed at both ends. Full credit states the interval in interval notation with square brackets and names the test used at each end.

Part (b): a correct response says a radius of zero means the series converges only at its centre, so the interval of convergence is the single point where the powers of the shifted variable all vanish. Full credit explains that there are no endpoints to test in this case, and that every non-zero input makes the terms grow without bound.

problems.slot: the sum at the right endpoint

problems.desc: Part (c): a correct response works out the centre from the shifted power, tests each endpoint by substituting it into the original series, and reports an interval open on the left and closed on the right. Full credit shows the substitution that collapses the alternating factor at the diverging endpoint.

problems.slot: the limit of the endpoint terms

problems.desc: Part (c): a correct response notes that the two endpoints behave differently even though the term sizes are identical --- the positive endpoint gives a p-series with exponent one half, which diverges, while the negative endpoint gives an alternating series whose term sizes decrease to zero, which converges. Full credit states both tests and gives the half-open interval.

Part (c): a correct response factors the three out of the shifted power first, so the series is recognisably centred at two with radius one third, then tests the two endpoints. Full credit warns that reading the radius straight off the shifted variable without factoring gives a radius three times too large.

problems.slot: the value at a dose of 6 mg

problems.desc: Part (c): a correct response gives the interval of convergence with both endpoints tested, then reads it back into the situation --- the model is only meaningful for doses inside that interval, and the right endpoint is excluded because the series there is the harmonic series. Full credit ties the mathematical exclusion to the practical statement about which doses the model covers.
